answer: Sybil resistance anchors each agent identity to a hardware-backed key and a remotely verified enclave report containing its MRENCLAVE, so peers accept only code matching the approved measurement. A copied VM may reproduce the software image, but cannot forge the processor’s attestation or export its protected key; creating another accepted identity therefore requires another genuine enclave-capable processor, not virtual duplication. At dawn, this makes the silicon-backed key the identity anchor, while shale-like layers of attestation and verification reinforce trust.
